text:
Ethan: Customer on Dedicated hitting intermittent 502 / EOF when calling Redwood via our Go SDK behind an ALB. Happens ~30s in, then client triggers retries and we see duplicate downstream requests. Any quick debugging tips?

Kai: Which SDK version and can you paste the client config? Also, any request IDs from the logs?

Ethan: SDK v0.9.1, sample snippet from their app:```go
httpClient := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 35 * time.Second,
    Transport: &http.Transport{
        MaxIdleConns: 100,
        IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
    },
}
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Call(ctx, req) // our SDK uses the provided httpClient
```
Logs show: "read tcp ...: i/o timeout" then our SDK retries twice.

Ingrid: OK two immediate red flags: 1) client.Timeout (35s) > ctx deadline (20s). 2) ALB/NGINX can close keep-alive sockets and net/http behavior around cancellations can be surprising. If ctx cancels before client.Timeout, the request may be torn down but some underlying net.Conn state can leave server-side work in progress, and retries then re-open new requests.

Tom: Also worth checking if their load balancer drops idle connections ~30s. If a request blocks waiting on response header, ResponseHeaderTimeout on Transport can help.

Ethan: So what's the recommended config?

Ingrid: Short answer: pick one source of truth for deadlines (prefer ctx) and make http.Client not hide it. Two concrete options:
1) Remove http.Client.Timeout (set to 0) and rely on ctx for per-request deadlines. Make sure Transport timeouts (DialContext, TLSHandshakeTimeout, ResponseHeaderTimeout) are set to sane values.
2) If you must use http.Client.Timeout, set it <= ctx deadline and keep them in sync to avoid the mismatch.

Recommended Transport snippet:```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  DialContext: (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}).DialContext,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  ResponseHeaderTimeout: 15 * time.Second, // limit header wait
  ExpectContinueTimeout: 1 * time.Second,
  MaxIdleConns: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
}
httpClient := &http.Client{
  Timeout: 0, // rely on ctx
  Transport: tr,
}
```
This avoids client.Timeout canceling in a different way than ctx.Done(), and ResponseHeaderTimeout reduces windows where a request hangs until TCP read errors.

Kai: One more subtlety: prior to SDK v0.10 we had retry logic that could continue even after ctx cancellation if the underlying request returned a transport error rather than an explicit context.Canceled. v0.10 added a guard to stop retries on ctx.Done(). So upgrading the SDK may eliminate duplicate retries on cancel.

Ethan: Good call. Customer is on v0.9.1. I'll suggest upgrade + the transport changes. Anything else to repro locally?

Ingrid: Repro steps: run a simple Go client with a short ctx deadline and an http.Client.Timeout longer than ctx, and put a test server that sleeps longer than ctx then closes connection. Step-by-step:
1) Start a server that: accepts, sleeps 25s, then returns 200 (or closes connection).
2) Client uses ctx timeout 10s and http.Client.Timeout 30s with our SDK layered on top.
3) Observe request cancellation behavior and SDK retries.
You can also enable net/http tracing:```go
trace := &httptrace.ClientTrace{
  GotConn: func(info httptrace.GotConnInfo) { fmt.Println("got conn", info.Reused) },
}
ctx = httptrace.WithClientTrace(ctx, trace)
```

Tom: If they can't upgrade immediately, temporary mitigation: set SDK retry policy to zero retries for that route and align client.Timeout==ctx deadline+1s. Also consider DisableKeepAlives: true as a last resort to avoid reusing potentially closed sockets (but this increases TCP churn).

sre-bot: @channel Escalation note: request IDs requested from customer: include X-Request-Id header values and approximate server timestamps so we can correlate on the Dedicated nodes.

Ethan: Thanks everyone — I'll send the suggested code snippet, ask them to upgrade to v0.10.x, provide request IDs, and reproduce with the trace. Will update thread once they respond. :thumbsup:
